newsitem.title: USA: CBOT SOYBEANS END SHARPLY LOWER ON WET FORECAST.
newsitem.headline: CBOT SOYBEANS END SHARPLY LOWER ON WET FORECAST.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures ended sharply lower with new crop months nearly limit down on forecasts for more rain across parched portions of the central U.S. Midwest, pit sources said.
"The (rainy) weather finally came in Sunday afternoon and Sunday night after a long weekend of waiting for it," said Jerry Gidel, analyst with Dean Witter in Chicago.

"There are prospects for some more rains continuing in certain spots through Wednesday," he added. "The corn market seems to feel some damage may have already been done but beans could see some improvement back above trend-line yields."
Soybean futures ended 29-1/2 to 16 cents per bushel lower with November down 27-1/2 at $6.10.

Weekend storms brought light rains to dry pockets of central Illinois and Indiana with only about 30 percent of the driest areas receiving more than 0.50 inch, Weather Services Corp said. But forecasts called for another 0.50 to 1.50 inch with 60 percent coverage across Missouri, Illinois, Indiana and Ohio over the next 24 to 48 hours, WSC said.
As of Sunday, WSC said rainfall in Peoria over the last 30 days totalled 2.89 inches, or 79 percent of normal. But in Indianapolis, the 30-day rainfall was still 10 pct of normal.

The market has been watching rainfall totals closely in recent weeks after sub-normal rains in July left some areas in dire need of moisture. August is considered the critical month for soybean development and stress from lack of moisture can lead to yield losses, traders said.

The trade awaited Tuesday's USDA crop production report, the first survey-based look at crop potential, but many sources said weather would continue to be the dominant factor. Analysts were expecting the report to show a record large soybean crop in the fields.
On the day, commission houses were largely on the sell side while commercials were light buyers. Traders said selling spilled over from the options pit where call selling was the featured play.
Refco Inc sold four million bushels November and bought two million November, Rand Financial sold 2.5 million November and R.J. O'Brien sold 1.5 million November, pit sources said.
Cargill Investor Services bought two million November, ADM bought 1.5 million November and Continental Grain bought one million November, traders said.
In options trade, Lind-Waldock sold 500 November $6.25 calls at 22 to 22-1/2 cents while Tradelink sold 300 November $6.50 calls at 15-3/4 cents.
Volatility in the November was pegged at 26 percent, down from 27 percent on Friday.
Soybean futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 32,000 contracts, compared with Friday's actual volume of 34,300.
